Ugmuls 5.5e Automation · Detailed Summary

Feats and spells.
Connected to the action.

Weapon masteries, feat benefits, shared unarmed options, and spell helpers that work with your native rolls and chat cards.

Automations → Weapon Masteries

Weapon masteries

The actor must have the mastery unlocked in its native D&D5e configuration. The main Effect Automation switch controls the group; turning it off greys out the individual options while preserving their selections.

  • Sap Applies on a hit and recommends disadvantage on the victim’s next attack.
  • Vex Applies after damage and recommends advantage on the attacker’s next attack against that target.
  • Slow Applies a non-stacking 10-foot speed reduction after damage, lasting until the source’s next turn starts.
  • Topple A hit-only card action prompts a Constitution save through the defender’s owner or GM, with a source-tracked Prone effect on failure.
  • Graze A miss automatically creates its flat damage card using the attack ability modifier and weapon damage type. It follows damage automation and supports Undo Damage. Undo hides that card and restores the linked attack’s Damage/Graze controls.

Push and Nick remain manual.

Cleave: follow the hit with another attack

A qualifying melee hit with an unlocked Cleave mastery offers a Cleave action on its attack chat card. Choose a different target and roll the separate attack. One use is shared across Cleave weapons each combat turn; canceling before the roll preserves it. Cleave cannot trigger itself.

Damage omits a positive ability modifier while keeping weapon magic bonuses and eligible features such as Rage. A negative ability modifier still applies. The module checks that the new target differs from the first; reach and distance stay at the table. If the original hit is later corrected, the GM manually undoes the Cleave.

Automations → Feats

Feat benefits,
right in the damage roll.

Your supported feat benefits appear where you use them: in the damage roll’s Configuration area. When an attack qualifies, the relevant options let you choose which benefits to use before rolling. The module handles the damage changes and tracks applicable once-per-turn limits, so you can focus on the attack.

  • Great Weapon Fighting Apply the fighting style to a qualifying melee attack made with a weapon held in two hands. Damage dice showing 1 or 2 count as 3. Two-Handed weapons qualify; Versatile weapons need a two-handed attack. The minimum also applies to attached bonus damage, both Savage Attacker dice sets, and critical-hit corrections.
  • Great Weapon Master Choose to add your proficiency bonus to damage on eligible Heavy-weapon hits made with the Attack action on your turn, including Heavy ranged weapons. Bonus-action and reaction attacks are excluded. The feat’s extra attack from Hew stays manual.
  • Savage Attacker Choose this benefit in the damage roll to roll the weapon’s damage dice twice and keep the higher total. Both sets remain visible in the result details. Its once-per-turn use is tracked automatically; canceling the prompt does not spend it, and Normal/Critical corrections after Undo keep the dice already rolled.
  • Grappler Choose Grapple during a qualifying Unarmed Strike’s damage roll to keep the attack’s damage and grapple once on your turn. Later Grapple attempts replace damage, and choosing Prone always replaces damage. The module also recommends advantage against a creature grappled by that attacker.
Unarmed combat & Grappler

Grapple, shove,
and keep control.

Qualifying action-based Unarmed, Empowered, and Elemental Strike hits offer Grapple and Shove (Prone) choices in damage Configuration. Select one to prompt the target’s saving throw and handle the matching effect using your table’s application settings. Bonus-action and reaction attacks are excluded.

These choices normally replace the strike’s damage. With the Grappler feat, you can keep the damage and make a Grapple attempt once on your turn. The module tracks that use; later Grapple attempts replace damage, and Shove (Prone) always replaces damage.

The screenshot shows Grappler alongside a Monk’s Stunning Strike. The Grappler benefit is available to any qualifying character with the feat.

Saving throws and effects

The target uses its better Strength or Dexterity saving throw, with Strength chosen on a tie. The save DC uses the attacker’s Strength, or Dexterity when Martial Arts allows it. These prompts use separate save cards, so the item’s existing Grapple and Shove activities stay available.

If Stunning Strike is also selected, it resolves first. A target that becomes Stunned automatically fails the linked Grapple save; otherwise, the module prompts the normal save. Grappled appears as a temporary effect on the token HUD without a timed expiry, and applied effects support Undo.

Automations → Spells

Cast the spell.
Keep the action moving.

React to a hit, strike your marked enemy, or bring extra elemental power to an attack. The spell’s options appear on the relevant card or damage roll, with resource tracking and results kept together.

  • Shield: turn a hit into a miss. When you’re hit and have a Reaction and a cast available, use Shield directly from the attack card. The module handles the Reaction and spell resource, using an available free cast before spending the lowest suitable spell slot. The attack updates against your new AC while keeping the original dice. If damage has already been applied, the GM can Undo it before making the correction.
  • Hex and Hunter’s Mark: make the marked hit count. Attack your marked target and choose the spell’s extra damage in the damage roll. The bonus rolls with the attack’s damage, while the module tracks your concentration and which creature is marked. Hunter’s Mark can also apply its effect automatically; Hex keeps its choice of affected ability.
  • Conjure Minor Elementals: bring the elements into the strike. When your single attack target is inside your active spell area, add the spell’s extra damage through the damage roll. Choose Acid, Cold, Fire, or Lightning; the module remembers your last choice and uses the damage for your cast level.
  • Buffs: cast it and share the benefit. Enable automatic buff application to give eligible recipients the spell’s included effects as part of the cast. Duration and concentration stay connected, including when an upcast spell such as Fly reaches more than one willing creature.

Eldritch Blast and Scorching Ray

Keep firing without keeping count. A Remaining Spell Attacks window tracks the shots granted by your character level or the spell level you chose. Select a target, click Attack, and choose a new target for the next shot—all from the same cast. Canceling a roll keeps that shot available, and the window closes when you’ve used them all.

When the spell lasts beyond the cast

Supported Player’s Handbook follow-ups are built into the Creature Effect Trigger library. Apply the native spell effect; its configured damage, healing, save, or optional escape prompt follows on later turns.

  • Repeat saves and action escapes. Fear, supported control spells, Entangle, Web, Ensnaring Strike, and Evard’s Black Tentacles receive their configured follow-ups. Optional escape cards wait for a player or GM to choose the action.
  • Recurring and delayed damage. Searing Smite and other supported lingering damage keep their turn timing. Melf’s Acid Arrow and Vitriolic Sphere handle their one-time delayed damage and then stop.
  • Recurring benefits. Supported Heroism and Regenerate effects prompt their configured temporary HP or healing.
  • Blink. Keep the initial card available to roll before ending the turn, with later end-turn prompts and a temporary ethereal effect.
  • Targeting-only areas. Supported Fear, Weird, and Confusion targeting areas can clear while their creature effects remain active.

Choose which recipes to enable, edit supported settings, or add custom entries. Native effect/stat changes remain intact. Movement, staged outcomes, counters, and situational decisions stay manual.
